claims.claim: Reviewers describe the mission structure as repetitive, consisting largely of fetching items or killing specific amounts of enemies.

citations.review_text:
This game feels like a clearly improved version of the first game. The dialogue is better, the characters talk more, the level design is miles ahead, and there are a bunch of new mechanics that make the whole thing feel less dry. The loot also feels better compared to the first game, and the bosses are generally more enjoyable too.

But — and it is a pretty big but — the mission design still can’t really escape the same problem. It’s still mostly “go kill this many enemies” or “go grab this thing and bring it back,” which was already my biggest issue with the first Borderlands. The better dialogue and stronger atmosphere make it less painful here, but the core problem is still sitting there.

The grind also feels heavier this time, and until I unlocked some actually useful skills, the combat could get genuinely rough. So yeah, it improves a lot of things from the first game, but it still carries enough of the same boring mission structure to hold it back.

6/10 - A little bit above average.

The first Borderlands I didn't manage to finish, the pacing and balancing was just awful. I was around level 19-20 when I foguht "RK5" and I wasn't able to get past it, since my level was too low but I definitely won't go backtracking and force myself through those awful and tedious sidemissions or even better start farming mobs so I can catch up with the levels. The enemey variety and design is lacking, aswell as the boss fights are boring, most of them are some kind of mech type enemy. The level design and all of the backtracking actually pissed me off.

The (back/pre)story is interesting and the writing is fun at times but can also get majorly annoying with some characters. The gun designs are like always genius and very fun to play around with. There are different mechanics now to be able to play with and combine the elements more, which is great and the movement is also pretty clean, just being too fast will mess with the Doppelgangers ability and makes the digi jacks constantly de- and respawn. 

Not a bad game, I just believe Borderlands 1 & 2 to be far superior, more polished, fun and exciting to play through. I would give it a mixed review, if that was an option but since I had to quit it and I'd rather recommend the first and second game, I will have to give it a negative review. 

Also changing up the terms of serivce decades after the orignial release is a very shady practice.

(7/10)

citations.review_text:
This game has been on my backlog for forever and you know I owe it to my younger self to actually finish the game he purchased and my oh my, of all the borderlands games I was really putting this one off. I think the elephant in the room is quite apparent with the mechanic of oxygen and the whole plot of being in space. I think realistically it’s just an annoying mechanic there for lore sake. When I first started out I really despised this mechanic, in fact I still do hate it with a passion. However, like insanity does to you, you sort of get used to it and find ways to adapt. 

I don’t like it because even with its redeeming factors it is still not as engaging as straight up gameplay. You have to either cycle oxygen machines or find cracks of oxygen to refill your tank, albeit not difficult but just a nuisance of gameplay. As much as I hate it, I will admit SOMETIMES it gets fun when you can slam down in the air and almost boost jump for some movement speed and then when you’re in the air floating to use your characters special ability that’s cool too. As much as of an inconvenience it is from normal mechanics you can tell that there was some consideration to make it bearable.  I much rather prefer some running and sliding and double jumps in gameplay rather than floating after every jump. There are many areas where you wont be needing to fill your tank but the whole game is in low gravity, so it’s really not HORRIBLY bad it’s not a deal breaker. It is an interesting mechanic for a borderlands game so I can’t hate too hard, I admire the willingness to try new things.

There is a lot of cool stuff in this game. I really like the enemy variety and enemy design and even the parts when it very clearly is trying to stretch the game with filler content it is redeemable in its writing or enemy variety. I didn’t necessarily do everything just cause I was really getting tired of the floating movement but even in the main story quest line alone, there’s a plethora of story a…

I'd argue this is the worst of all the Borderlands games. The story is fine, most of the characters are fun to play, the environments are okay and the oxygen mechanics are interesting. What kills the enjoyment of the game for me is the low power level of everything making progression feel slow, and the zero gravity environments making looting frustrating. I didn't like this game when I played it on Xbox years ago and I like it even less now.

citations.review_text:
I think the main reason I did not finish this game until 2026, despite replaying Borderlands 1 and 2 multiple times, is that, while it’s not a terrible game, everything The Pre-Sequel does, Borderlands 2 does better. I like the idea of taking the same game engine and making more of what players loved about 2 but:
- The writing feels like a bunch of people who read a lot about Borderlands humor and story studied really hard and made a half-convincing fan tribute.
- The gameplay takes the refined, polished feel of 2 and adds a bunch of features that do almost nothing for the gameplay loop except add minor tedium.
- The maps and level design are so overdone that I was dreading seeing the surface of Elpis again whenever the story took me back there.

Overall, I would skip it and play Borderlands 2 again.

Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel has some good ideas, but overall it’s easily the weakest main Borderlands game for me. The low gravity movement and laser weapons are fun, and the Vault Hunters are some of the best in the franchise, with great build variety. Handsome Jack’s story is also interesting and adds a lot to the Borderlands universe. Unfortunately, the game is dragged down by its terrible pacing and map design. Most areas feel huge, empty, repetitive, and visually boring, making exploration and constant backtracking feel like a chore. The level progression is awkward, and many side quests just send you through the same dull areas again and again. I also didn’t enjoy the Claptastic Voyage DLC nearly as much as most people seem to. The bullet sponge enemies and chaotic combat made it more frustrating and messy than memorable. The lack of meaningful endgame content makes things even worse, giving very little reason to keep playing after finishing the main content. There are definitely good mechanics and characters here, but they aren’t enough to overcome the repetitive environments, frustrating pacing, weak endgame, and tedious quest design. It’s the only Borderlands game I’ve finished and never wanted to play again. 3/10

If you liked the other games you'll like this one too. The game mechanics on this game are a great improvement on BL2's. My only gripes were with:
Map design. Most maps were meh and the backtracking and lack of fast travel locations made me want to stop playing at times.
And the writing. It felt a bit "off" compared to BL2. I can't think of a single joke from this game that I could legitimately call *memorable.*
Edit: The DLC Claptastic Voyage absolutely made up for whatever quarrels I had with this game. It was amazing.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the addition of laser weapons, cryo damage, and the weapon grinder as notable mechanical updates.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel: A Good Game Stuck in Borderlands 2's Shadow[/h1]

[h2]TL;DR[/h2]

Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel is a good Borderlands game, but coming directly after Borderlands 2 makes its shortcomings difficult to ignore.

Low gravity, Cryo weapons, lasers, Oz kits, and some excellent Vault Hunters give the formula enough new ideas to feel worthwhile. The story also provides an interesting look at Handsome Jack before Borderlands 2.

Unfortunately, Elpis is less interesting to explore than Pandora, missions drag more often, the humor and supporting cast are less consistent, and there simply is not as much worthwhile content.

[b]7/10: Definitely a step down from Borderlands 2, but still a good time.[/b]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Gameplay & Vault Hunters[/h2]

The Pre-Sequel is fundamentally built on Borderlands 2, which gives it an excellent foundation. The shooting, randomized loot, skill trees, co-op, and general progression are immediately familiar.

The biggest changes come from Elpis itself. Low gravity lets you stay airborne longer, Oz kits provide bonuses and oxygen, and ground slams add another option during combat. Oxygen sounds annoying on paper, but it is plentiful enough that I rarely found it intrusive.

[b]Cryo might be my favorite addition.[/b]

Freezing enemies solid and shattering them is incredibly satisfying, while laser weapons add some genuinely fun options to the arsenal.

The Vault Hunters are also excellent. Athena, Wilhelm, Nisha, Claptrap, Doppelganger Jack, and Aurelia all offer distinct playstyles, and their personalities come through more during missions because they actually respond to other characters.

The downside is that much of Borderlands 2's jank remains. Vehicles are awkward, enemy AI has its moments, and inventory management is still clunky.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Elpis & Mission Design[/h2]

Elpis is a great idea for a setting. Looking back at Pandora from its moon while bouncing across low-gravity landscapes immediately gives…

Doing a chronological binge re-playthrough of the entire franchise (not tales)

This is definitely the worst one, and it's not close. This is the only one I've felt the need to write a review on.

Pros: 
-It's basically built off Borderlands 2, the best one, so it feels similar in many ways. 
-The one DLC it has is pretty interesting (holodome isn't real just like moxxi's dome isn't real in BL1)
-Energy guns are pretty cool
-Aimhacks as a cowboy are pretty cool
-Seeing Handsome Jack's backstory and abrupt slip into Machiavellism is pretty cool

Cons: 
-It's basically built off Borderlands 2, but 99% of the changes or additions are useless or make the game worse than BL2
-low gravity jumping. I could seriously write a dissertation on how terrible this mechanic is. 
   -The better Oz kits typically require you to be in the air to get the best combat bonuses. Of couse, if I get +50% crit damage in the air, I'm gonna be in the air as much as possible. But so much vertical movement and aiming in a shooter feels really bad.
   -When you're in the air, it's not uncommon for an enemy, like a boss, to knock you back, off a cliff, into a death plane and just die. 
   -Managing O2 levels feels really bad. It's so rare that your oxygen ever runs out but, when you're on a platforming section, and you mess up a jump a couple of times, you need to regen oxygen and keep trying, which only adds to the frustration. Also there is A LOT of platforming in this game. 
-Laser weapons feel really overpowered when they work, but they're completely useless against bosses that stay far away because laser weapons have a limited range. If you've built your character around lasers, then run into a boss that's too far away, you're cooked. Better go farm or buy a different kind of gun that can reach the boss.
-The dune buggy is an awfully designed vehicle that never should have been shipped with the game. I know they become irrelevant pretty quickly but, for the limited time where they're necessar…

Borderlands The Pre Sequel is a lot like the uncle you keep hearing about. You know the one. He cut off your family and lives a healthy, active and unique lifestyle, which your family keeps describing as boring or "the worst one in the family".

The truth is that this is most likely overall, the most well rounded game in the series and it could have been even better than 2 if the studio was given time to finish all the DLC and content. The content that we did receive is, undoubtedly in my opinion the single best DLC in Borderlands history, the best story in the series and absolutely the best vault hunter lineup in the series and the rest dont even come close. 

This is really the only borderlands game ive played where I havent felt like one or two of the characters are bad. Yes, there is Wilhelm, but he isnt bad. The lineup is just so busted this time that hes the most normal out of all of them, and thats very usual for the introductory soldier class in all of the games. All of the characters are extremely fun to use and viable in the end game. And theyre all incredibly distinct and unique.

The game introduces new mechanics that were quite overlooked or viewed negatively on release but now I think are viewed normally. New melee mechanics such as the slam, new weapons class such as the laser, the grinder which allows you to combine weapons and receive higher rarity weapons including legendaries, and the Zero G environment, which adds very fun and speedy movement using the oxygen kits that you find. And all of these are very fun features and they really felt fun after BL2.

The DLC is the best in the series, alongside the story.  The story is never anything to boast about in any of the borderlands games, but this time...magically, everything is fine. Funny jokes, funny characters with humor that isnt always screaming in your face, and the most character development in the series - all of your vault hunters have unique dialogue associated with them, and they are refer…

While the Borderland Pre-Sequel adds a lot of cool new concepts, it ultimately feels like a step down from Borderlands 2.  On the positive side, I enjoyed the new character skill trees, the introduction of laser weapons, and the low-gravity gameplay (kind of reminded me of Destiny's Warlock jump).  On the downside, the game feels like it has a lot less content, less endgame bosses, and just has a lot of collision bugs.  I had fun with it, but this will probably be the last Borderlands game I play.

Okay so there's a lot of problems with this game sadly. The pacing, the writing (at times), the level design, the voice acting, performance (looking at you PhysX) and the lack of content. There's good parts and it shines above BL2 sometimes, so I'd still recommend it, but it's hard to ignore the wasted potential. The main reason for this is Australia 2K shutting down and the near-abandonment by Gearbox.

This game could have been really good, and I think this is most apparent in the Claptastic voyage DLC, it felt like a significant improvement over the base game and it's a shame BLTPS couldn't get more development time.

I'd still recommend this game, but it's replayability feels considerably more stunted than BL2, TVHM (2nd playthrough) feels like a slog that I wouldn't recommend.

I recommend it, BUT:

1) I installed it after playing BL3. Compared to that the gameplay feel very clunky
2) Ground vehicle steering with only mouse aiming is VERY unintuitive. The moon buggy stops at everything protruding from the ground a little.
3) Low gravity SLOWS the action - it takes forever to get close to the enemies. Forget using shotgun. Sniper rifle rules them all. 
4) No sliding
5) Story is maybe a little more interesting but nothing to be amazed by... BL series was never about story. It is about action. And the action pace here is like turn based strategy game.
6) Weapons have no such variety like in BL3. GOLD and PURPLE weapons are very hard to come by.
7) No automatic items pickup. U have to press E for a long time to pick up everything around U.
8) No fast travel from anywhere on the map. U have to go to the right fast travel station. There is only one on each location.
9) It is faster to Quit the game to the main menu and RESUME than jump in zero gravity back to the start of the map
10) VERY NICE usage of PhySX NVIDIA physics of debris. So, If you have RTX 4k or older U will get very nice effects. Sorry 5k users :(.
11) Game freezes from time to time :/

citations.review_text: The pre-sequel is shadowed by what could have been had 2K Australia not gone under mid dev. At its current state it's still a great game for a playthrough or two, damaged by the fact that it has no endgame, a staple in the franchise. The environments are cool and unique, the low gravity mechanic is fun (albeit annoying at times) and the Vault Hunters might be the most fun in the series. The claptastic voyage dlc is incredible and I can't help but wonder what would happen if we had gotten full post launch content support. Grab it on sale, which it goes often these days.

This was my second game on the Borderlands universe.  It basically follows the same formula as Borderlands 2, with some nice improvements. Set mostly on the moon, the introduction of low gravity and oxygen management makes the game more interesting. It changes how you move, fight, and approach encounters, adding verticality and a slightly more tactical rhythm to combat. Jumping higher, slamming down on enemies, and keeping an eye on your oxygen levels gives the familiar Borderlands gameplay a refreshing layer of variety. Everything else will feel comfortably familiar: the cartoony art style, the constant jokes, the ridiculous amount of weapons, and a story that fills in some background rather than stealing the spotlight. There’s less of a “new discovery” feeling compared to Borderlands 2, but that’s more a consequence of familiarity than a flaw in design. For fans of Borderlands, it’s an easy recommendation,  especially when picked up on sale. A solid 8/10

If this were an expansion pack, it would probably be in my top 3 of all time. Alas, it's a standalone game... which will be demoted to 'glorified DLC' for the duration of this review.

All jokes aside (but not really), this is basically BL2 with some new mechanics, a new world (Australia), and a new coat of paint. There are also some 'gimmicks', like what is probably the coolest element ever introduced to the series (Cryo) (bad dum tss), and a machine that lets you recycle loot, although none of them are as relevant as the fact that Australia was finally represented in the Borderlands universe.

I'll be reviewing this as a sequel to Borderlands 2, but if you must know, it's a pretty good game by itself. It does its own thing well enough, so if you're into looter shooters, go get it.

Positives:

- Australia
- It's on the moon, and low gravity adds more mobility options, and a new, albeit thin layer of complexity to combat
- Cryo is absolutely based and busted as hell, and lets you do fun things like freeze enemies mid air then letting gravity do the rest; laser weapons are a tad clunky to use but still a good addition
- The Grinder, even if awkward at times, added an extra dimension to looting, making even the trashiest of items worth picking up
- One of the best final bosses, or maybe bosses overall in all of Borderlands, to the point where I actually enjoyed fighting it (seriously, if all bosses in the series were like this, I would actually look forward to fighting them)
- The writing in general was on par, if not better than Borderlands 2's, and adds some needed context to some of the characters' actions

Negatives:

- Australia; ok srsly now, I get that the devs are Australian and proud, but they could've instructed their voice actors to sound a bit more neutral, as it's very jarring hearing OI ♥♥♥♥ M8 CRIKEY OI G'DAY M8 ♥♥♥♥ CRIKEY in a space game

[b]Introduction :[/b]
Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel, sorti en octobre 2014, est un spin-off développé par 2K Australia en collaboration avec Gearbox. Comme son nom l'indique, l'histoire se situe entre le premier et le deuxième opus et raconte l'ascension de Handsome Jack, le légendaire méchant de Borderlands 2, à l'époque où il n'était encore qu'un simple employé d'Hyperion. On incarne cette fois l'un des futurs sbires de Jack et on pose le pied sur Elpis, la lune de Pandore, ainsi que sur la station spatiale Helios. Le gros twist de gameplay : la faible gravité lunaire et la gestion de l'oxygène, qui transforment les gunfights habituels de la saga en affrontements bien plus verticaux.

[b]Ce que j'ai aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🌙 La faible gravité change vraiment la donne, on bondit sur des dizaines de mètres et on peut écraser les ennemis en retombant, ça dynamise des fusillades qu'on connaissait par cœur
[*]🤖 Claptrap jouable, c'est l'idée géniale du jeu : son arbre de compétences totalement aléatoire et imprévisible est un délire permanent pour qui aime le chaos
[*]😂 L'humour reste la marque de fabrique Borderlands, les dialogues et l'accent australien des PNJ font mouche, on rigole franchement
[*]❄️ Les armes laser et les dégâts de glace (cryo) sont une vraie nouveauté qui renouvelle l'arsenal et la façon de gérer les hordes
[*]🎭 Voir l'origine de Handsome Jack et comprendre comment il bascule du « gentil » au tyran de BL2 est un régal pour qui a fait le 2
[*]💨 La gestion de l'oxygène ajoute une couche tactique, on cherche les bouches d'O2 et on utilise les double-sauts boostés pour se repositionner
[*]🔫 Tout le loot-shooter qui fait l'ADN de la saga est là : des millions d'armes, du farm de boss, du coop quatre joueurs ultra addictif
[/list]

[b]Ce que j'ai moins aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🗺️ Les décors lunaires gris et répétitifs lassent vite, on regrette la variété visuelle de Pandore dans les autres opus
[*]🐛 Techniquement le jeu reprend les qualités de BL2 mais aussi qua…

It's like Borderlands 2's little brother, the same DNA but not as good. That being said the o2 kit adding double jumping is a great addition, and the space theme is great.

Rating: 7.5/10

claims.claim: Reviewers report that visible and invisible ledges, as well as terrain features, frequently block movement and impede traversal on foot and in vehicles.

citations.review_text:
Overall the Pre-Siquel feels like a cheap DLC of the second game. Gunplay isn't very good either with its outdated sway and recoil mechanics. Movement is supposed to be fun on paper. Flying around, shooting from above and stuff. But it's just slow and boring. Not to mention the numerous visible and invisible ledges that stop you way too often. Even the vehicles are not spared from this.
It has some stronger points like level design and story, but boring gameplay quickly descourages from exploring them.

Edit after 100%:  Completionists will not have a good time here - grindy, tidious, boring achievements

I just went through this game again.  Borderlands Pre-Sequel hasn't significantly changed from Borderlands 1 or 2.  It still has major problems with invisible walls and stops your movements for no valid reason when walking / running between elevations.  It still has insufferable delays and bad targeting when picking up items.  It still cuts the timer down every time you lose all your HP, so free-for-alls are death, and sniping is the only legitimate way to pay the game (particularly with constant-streaming laser weapons).  The classes, again,  aren't as good as the B1 classes.

In addition, most of the game is set in low gravity, which means it takes MUCH longer to get from one place to another.  There are also lots of areas where there is no oxygen, and you have to do a lot of backtracking to refresh your air (or die).  The game also goes vertical, so it takes even longer to explore an entire area.  And you can get stuck in areas with no way out.  There are fewer checkpoints, so it takes a LOT longer to get anywhere.  There are also no Fast Travel stations in some areas, which is maddening.  The weapon balance in this game is steered to the low end, too - I only managed to finish the game with 3 weapons, all purple.  The first time I ever played this, it was damned near impossible to finish it.  As I said in previous Borderlands reviews, the game keeps getting worse.

The absolute worst part of this game is that they added platforming.  This means you have to time your jumps just right, and air-boost at just the right times, or you will fall into abysses and die - and have to go back to the nearest checkpoint, which can be all the way across the map.  It's simply not worth it to explore every nook and cranny, when a missed boost - or an added one - means death, and losing money to add insult to injury.

This game is basically just like Borderlands 1 with a slightly better storyline (Jack is one of the best-written antagonists ever), but that really isn't enough to …

citations.review_text: Numerous new bugs have destroyed the co-op experience in 2026 and it is effectively a single player game. My friends and I can no longer play this together.

So.....this was a difficult one as the premise is interesting but executed poorly. The repetitive nature of guns is a reoccurring issue we ran into many of the same guns over and over again. Found numerous bugs with quest givers not accepting quests and the many many tedious achievements AND LACK OF F**KING GAME SYNC BETWEEN PLAYERS. I'd recommend it on a heavy discount for the completionists collection but beware its a dredge as the views and maps aren't very different from each other. I don't know why 2K decided to make all the moon dwellers Australian as Joke but it sure wears thin far as a Joke. As I said heavy discount and I'd recommend this game but its definably one of the weaker titles in the  borderlands series.
